definition: How a BOM line takes its colours. Three types: Base Colour (apparel colours used directly), Table (the user maps each apparel colour to a material colour from the material colour master) and None (no colour).
How a BOM line takes its sizes. Three types: Base Size (apparel sizes used directly), Table (the user maps apparel sizes to material sizes) and None (no size).
The colours of the apparel are used directly for the material: the material is needed in the same colours as the garment.

The user maps each apparel colour to a material colour. It tells the system "buy the fabric in this colour to achieve the apparel in that colour". The apparel colour master and the fabric (or any raw material) colour master can differ, so this map bridges them.
The material has no colour. It is the same for every apparel colour (for example a polybag).
The apparel sizes are used directly for the material: the material comes in the same sizes as the garment.
The user maps each apparel size to a material size (or leaves it unused), when the material is not sized like the garment.
The material has no size. It is the same for every apparel size.
The unit in which the material is kept and counted in stock (warehouse, GRN, issue). Stock balances are held in this unit.
The unit in which the BOM states how much of the material one garment uses (Cons Qty, Final Consumption).
The unit in which the material is bought from the supplier (RMPO, price). When it differs from the Consumption UOM a conversion factor turns the purchase price into the Cons UOM Price.
Captures the raw materials needed to make one apparel, how much of each (consumption), at what cost, and the price at which the apparel is to be sold.
A BOM is maintained version-wise. Each version carries its own cost sheet with a currency and a date and time, so older versions and their costs stay available.

The BOM marked as standard, either by selecting the star or by choosing the Standard BOM option while creating it. It is treated as the master BOM and creates the Budget: every other BOM of the apparel is compared against it as the budget.
The BOM used to produce an order. Its costs are compared with the Standard BOM, which acts as its budget.
A BOM can be made by copying from a template or by copying from an item (an existing BOM).
A setting that nominates the master cost sheet of the BOM.

The BOM carries a User Group and a Purchase Officer. If they are not filled, the indent generated after MRP comes in Inactive status. It must be activated from the User Indent list or the Indent list before MRP and the other adjustments can be done on it.

term: Article Code and Article Name generation
definition: The article code and article name of a techpack are generated in one of two ways: Automatically or Manually. Manually, the user types the code or name. Automatically, the system builds it from the rules set up in Admin › System Coding.
Go to Admin › System Coding and search for Article Code or Article Name. Each has its own definition and both vary by category (for example Textiles/Fabric).

A definition has a Category and a Logic (Manual or Automatic). For automatic logic each rule picks a Material Type, Product Group and Sub Category (or "ALL Other"), then lists code sections in Sort order (10, 20, 30…). The code is the sections joined in that order.

Running MRP for Level 1 (the garment) for the full quantity also generates the indents for the child level (the raw materials of the BOM) in the same run: child quantity = Level 1 quantity × BOM Final Consumption. If the parent changes later, re-running MRP carries the change into the child indent.

Every MRP level (parent and child) can take a negative quantity (for example -500). The level where you enter it is the level that changes. To reduce or cancel a child indent, the negative has to be entered at its parent level: that lowers the parent quantity MRP acts on, so once MRP is re-run the child indent is reduced by the same share (any change in the parent followed by a re-run of MRP impacts the child indent), and taking off the whole parent quantity (-500 of 500) cancels it.

A negative quantity entered at a child level changes only that child level. It does not reach the parent and does not cancel the child indent by itself: cancelling a child indent needs the negative at the parent level.

A Sales Order (Main OC) holds Deliveries (Delivery OCs). Each delivery holds one or more Articles, and each article holds a Colour/Size breakup with selling price. The list shows one row per order and article, with the order number repeated.

The creation screen is one transaction page with Order Information (Sales Order No, Category, Buyer, Buyer Division/Dept, Order Season), Other Details, Delivery and Items, Instructions, Documents and History. The title reads Add Sales Order when new, Edit Sales Order when revising and Sales Order when only viewing.

Fills a new order in one of two ways: copy from the Buyer Default Template (the template of the selected buyer, from Buyer Master › Default tab) or copy from an Existing Sales Order (all details including quantities; search by order number or style; the last 10 orders are listed).

Mode A is Style + Color + Size: one row per unique combination with Number of Sets, Size, Selling Price, Value and Total Quantity. Mode B is Style-wise grouping: one group per style with Color/Size, Quantity, Selling Price, Value, BOM and Total Quantity. A TBA colour/size line is always created by default.

Inherited from the Tech Pack, never typed on the order. It decides at which level the selling price is kept: Article (one price), Color (a price per colour, average shown), Size (a price per size, average shown) or Color/Size (a price per combination, average shown).

Driven by Price Per. The base selling price comes from the Tech Pack. A positive value is an upcharge, a negative value is a discount, and the final selling price is read-only: Base Selling Price ± Upcharge/Discount. Only when the setting "Enable Base Price and Upcharge in Summary OC" is ON; when OFF the Tech Pack price goes straight into Selling Price.

When several approved and accepted BOMs exist, the order picks the selling price of the latest accepted BOM. If the user selects a BOM for the article from the dropdown, the price of that BOM is used.

Shown under the article. Non-textile: taken from the Tech Pack, otherwise blank. Textile/fabric: taken first from the Linked Customer table for the selected buyer, then from the Tech Pack, otherwise blank. Whether the value can be edited follows the BSR configuration.

Extra Production % entered at the article header adds a percentage on top of the order quantity and is shown in its own grid under the Quantity Breakup on the Proforma Invoice and Print page. Additional Quantity is added in a separate tab with its own quantity, selling price and a reason from a dropdown. Both can be excluded from MRL generation by a setting, and the planned (PD) quantity must still equal the total OC quantity.

Chosen per article: Solid Color / Solid Size (a single colour and size, existing popup), Solid Color / Assorted Size (a PP column; one colour only, ratios across sizes) and Multiple Prepack (PP ratios across colours and sizes). Price Per and its dropdown are not shown here, they come from the Tech Pack.

A tool that adds another, independent quantity grid under the same article, with a count of how many were added. It is enabled only for Solid Color / Assorted Size and Multiple Prepack. The packing type of an added grid is frozen, and each added grid can be deleted.

A size categorisation by inside leg length (Petite, Missy, Regular, Tall, Long, Short) so the same waist size can come in several length variants. Values are kept in the Size Master and chosen per size in the Color/Size popup.

A delivery cannot mix kit and non-kit articles. The first article chosen fixes the type and later selections show only that type. Kit articles are shown in grid view only, with the kit name and kit ID and an indicator.

Adds a new delivery by the Add Delivery button or the + beside Deliveries in the left panel (the + is for additional deliveries). The popup has Delivery Information and Article Information, all blank and editable, and the line shows Pending until confirmed, then Confirmed.

Copies a delivery of the same order from the Action column or the left panel. A new blank delivery opens with the style already filled; delivery number, date and lines must be entered again, and everything stays editable.
Removes one or several ticked deliveries after a confirmation that names them (for example Delivery 001, 002 and 003). A delivery article can be deleted until its GMPO or ASN has been created.
Splits a delivery quantity by Percentage (default) or by Quantity from the sidebar of the edit page. Only the delivery information is shown, and Save replaces Confirm while splitting.

Tick one or more deliveries, open the context menu, choose Cancel and enter remarks (required). After "Do you want to Cancel the selected Delivery Order(s)?" and OK the status turns Cancelled (red) and the remarks show on hover and in History.
Same steps as cancel with the Close option. The status turns Closed (orange); the delivery stays in the list and the remarks are kept.

Only a closed delivery can be reopened. Choose Reopen, enter remarks and confirm; the status becomes Open (green) and the delivery is editable again. On a delivery that is not closed the system says "Please Uncheck Confirmed Delivery OC."

A delivery is refused when Delivery Buyer Order Ref, Buyer Delivery Date, OC Delivery Date and Mode of Shipment are all the same as an existing one. If any one of them differs the delivery is allowed.
When a confirmed order has been revised and a delivery is kept in draft, the Delete button is disabled on both the list and the edit page.

Every action is logged with date, time, user and remarks: status updates, approval trail (approver name, status, comments), comments and notes, and delivery actions such as "Delivery Order Closed (1) 12:22:02 PM 26/12/2026 Nishant Test Case". When an order is sent for approval the approver name shows in the timeline.

Grid context-menu tool, enabled only when a confirmed order is revised. It opens the latest version in the Modified tab; versions are chosen from a multi-select header dropdown and load on the All, Modified and Inserted/Deleted tabs. Rows appear only when something changed: Version Change, Revision Authorised By, Reason for Revision, Delivery Name, header changes, Total Qty and UOM, Total Value and Currency, and quantity details (article, colour and size, qty, price, value).

term: Reason for revision and Revision Authorized By
definition: Both are mandatory text fields shown when the user chooses Revise from the grid context menu.

Grid context menu › Cancel opens a warning that all Delivery OCs of the Main OC will be cancelled, then a mandatory remarks popup. On OK the order and all its deliveries are cancelled and the status becomes Cancelled. An order that is Saved, Cancelled or Closed cannot be cancelled: "You cannot cancel a Saved, Cancelled, or Closed Order."
Grid context menu › Close opens a popup with mandatory remarks; on Close Order the status becomes Closed. A Cancelled or Closed order cannot be closed: "You cannot close a Cancelled or Closed Order."

Moves quantity of a delivery to a new delivery or to an existing delivery of the same order. Target Sales Order = New: the target lookup is frozen, a Draft delivery is created on Load with all delivery information, articles, colours and sizes, prices and instructions copied, and the Buyer Order Reference is left blank for the user. Existing: pick one eligible target delivery and the quantities and values of both are recalculated.

A target delivery must belong to the same Sales Order, buyer and style/OC, be Draft or editable, not Cancelled and not Closed, and the user must be able to modify it. The source delivery can never be its own target.

By Quantity the entered quantity is spread proportionately over the selected article colour/size lines and taken off the source. By Percentage each line moves Existing Quantity × Percentage ÷ 100, rounded to the UOM precision. Quantity must be above zero and not above the delivery quantity; percentage above 0 and not above 100.

A delivery can get Notes from the Notes action. The dropdown lists only active notes from Sales › Codes › OC Notes; each Save is its own "OC Note Added" entry in the activity timeline with note, user and time. Update Notes uploads an Excel to set notes on many orders. A deleted note stays in the timeline but cannot be picked again.

Proforma Invoice opens a page at delivery level. Print opens a page grouped by Delivery, Market or Destination. Both show a Sub Total column in the sales order currency and an Extra Production % grid under the Quantity Breakup.
Header context menu › Run MRP opens the level-wise material screen: MRL for a cost sheet order, the Pending MRP List for a BOM order.
Exports to Excel only what the list currently shows, respecting filters, sorting and page size.

term: ASN, GDN, invoice and dispatch links
definition: Under the Order Qty column ASN and GDN hyperlinks open a popup with the ASN and GDN quantities of that delivery. The Sales Invoice number opens Sales Invoice Detail (invoice no, date, qty, value). Dispatch opens the Buyer Dispatch Note: destination first, then dates, then articles, then a dispatch allocation grid and Material Re-Allocation with reserve and free stock.

term: BOM Information and Material Requirement Status
definition: The context menu opens the BOM of the delivery style in view mode, and the Material Status popup of the style in that delivery.
Edits Buyer Delivery Date, OC Delivery Date, Buyer Order Date, PCD Date, PO Packet Date and GAC Date in a grid without an OC revision. After Save the new dates show on the OC and the related screens.

A master keeps days against shipment mode, order company, buyer and buyer department. When the Buyer Delivery Date is entered the OC Delivery Date fills automatically that many days earlier. OC Delivery Date otherwise always follows the Buyer Delivery Date.

Set per approver: 0 means the document never goes for approval, -1 means it always does, and a limit above 0 means it goes for approval only when the order value exceeds the limit (a value equal to the limit does not).

The creator names one approver. After Confirm a popup sends the order for approval; the approver finds it under Home › Approval Centre › Sales Order › Pending Approval. Approval makes the status Confirmed; the history keeps approver, status, comments, date and time.

Enabled for the document Sales Order in the Multi-Level Approval Settings (beside Purchase Order From Buyer). Creator → first approver (chosen by the creator) → next approver (chosen by the first, ending with a final approver). The order stays pending after each intermediate approval and becomes Confirmed only after the final one.
More than one approver can be assigned so a missing approver does not block the order. One of them is the default shown in the dropdown, the others are selectable.

term: Auto price pickup from cost sheet
definition: On a new OC the selling price comes from the confirmed cost sheet or BOM for the style and destination. Prices are destination-wise in the Cost Sheet Summary.

A mismatch between the OC selling price and the cost sheet/BOM price marks the record Desynced (blue). The Desync tool in the Sales Order List (enabled only on a mismatch) syncs it: status Sync (green) and the OC price is overwritten with the cost sheet/BOM price, which is always the source of truth. A hyperlink opens OC Details with destination, delivery date, colour/size, OC price and cost sheet price. Needs the setting "OC Price Validation with selling price in cost sheet" ON.

term: Update OC with latest cost sheet price
definition: If the cost sheet price is revised and confirmed (for example 10 to 15), this action fetches the latest confirmed price and updates the OC selling price from 10 to 15.

Confirming an order with Fulfilment Type Back Order shows a New PO (GMPO) option on the OC, also reachable from the GMPO Pending List. From the GMPO the user generates the Material Requirement List (MRL), which creates the material indents from the BOM.

For Order Type CM the OC Factory field is shown as Supplier (a mandatory dropdown from the Supplier Master, filtered by category). Confirming creates a GMPO per delivery for that supplier, listed in the GMPO Pending List, and the style indent appears in the Pending MRP List. The GMPO price is the Purchase Price (entered per colour or per size next to Selling Price), not the Selling Price. MRP fulfils the purchase demand automatically and the demand is locked.

Confirming a Purchase fulfilment order creates style indents in Indent Management. A manufacturing order can also be bought finished: after MRP Level 1 is the Style Indent and Level 2 the Material Indents, and the Purchase Demand field at Level 1 holds the style quantity to buy directly. On the next MRP run the material indents are reduced, or removed when the whole quantity is purchase demand, and an RMPO is raised on the style indent.

An MTS order (Order Type Make to Stock, Fulfilment Manufacturing) is produced and received into inventory, and no Sales ASN is created. A customer order with Fulfilment Type Purchase Order then takes that stock in Material Allocation (Sales Order Adjustment): the screen lists source MTS order, item, warehouse, available, allocated and balance quantity; allocation cannot exceed the available stock, and the same stock can serve several orders until it reaches zero.

Before TP mapping the Order Company maps the Buyer (end customer) in Company Info and the Execution Company maps the Supplier. The mapping sits in FA › Master Definitions › AR Masters › Transfer Price › Default Transfer Price Mapping. Backward TP uses buyer, order and execution company and division, effective date, end customer and Price Applicable On (Default Margin % on FOB, Default Margin % on Material Cost in Internal Costsheet, Default Margin Rate, Default Selling Price). Forward TP uses based-on transaction, auto transactions, companies and divisions, supplier, fulfilment type and dispatch site.

The order starts in the Order Company: Techpack, OC, approved costing and GMPO there; the system then creates Techpack, OC and an open costing in the Execution Company. After local purchase articles, costing approval, manual BOM, MRL, production, FPO and FPPO, Sales ASN and FG dispatch, the system creates the Sourcing ASN, Inter Purchase Invoice and Sales ASN in the Order Company.

The order starts in the Execution Company: the OC takes the Execution Company default selling price and the system creates a GMPO/OC with the .Auto suffix in the Order Company. After procurement, production and Sales ASN (with execution company and ETD/ETA), the system creates the GMPO GRN, Supplier Invoice and OC Sales ASN in the Order Company; the user creates the Consignment Sales Invoice and does clearing and posting, and the system creates the Sales Invoice in the Execution Company.

A TNA template is attached per delivery or, in the list, Main OC wise (a count of articles with an info icon) or Style wise. Once confirmed it cannot be edited directly: Update TNA removes the template and reopens selection (only if one was attached), and Delete Track removes it (alert if none). Copy Below copies a template down. If an article is in several deliveries the earliest delivery date is used. Auto TNA attaches templates from TNA › Codes › Auto TNA Attachment Rules, still to be confirmed by the user.

An electronic buyer PO imported and turned into a Buyer Order by configured mapping. Admin › Integration › Package Configuration (company, entity type, transaction type, package type Import/Export, SSIS package, folder path, active) and Package Mapping (WFX field, package field, mapping resolution type Data, System Data, User Input, Review & Create, Review & Map, Review & Resolve, Review & Select, plus dependency, mandatory, visibility, editable and sort order). On Sales › Purchase Order from Buyer › EDI Buyer PO: choose buyer and package, Import, pick the Excel file, Process Package, fix items in Error Resolution, then Create Transaction.

New (newly created orders), Revision (existing orders updated by EDI), On Hold (held manually, with Unhold) and Processed (confirmed). Delivery Detail opens the delivery level view and then the colour/size view; Confirm finalises the order and Export downloads the processed data.
Fields created in Sales › Codes › Tracking Fields sync into the Flex Fields of the Other Details section.

term: Buyer Block Booking on the order
definition: Block booking type is Projection or Reservation. The BOM column lists approved BOMs of the article: with a BOM selected the material popup is filled from it and has no Add to Catalog tool; without one Add from Catalog is available. Generate Indent Requirement creates an Adhoc indent. Entering colour/size quantity is mandatory before Link Buyer Block Booking.

The list of every material one garment needs – how much of each (consumption with wastage), in which colour and size, at what price – plus the routing (processes) and the cost sheet. MRP and FPO use its Final Consumption to plan and issue material.
The master record of an article in WFX: an Apparel techpack for the garment, and a Fabric or Trims techpack for each raw material.
The finished garment, e.g. Adi TShirt (NIS-59) or Flannel Shirt Adi (NIS-58), with buyer, colour card, size range and purchase UOM.
The Cost tab of the BOM: material cost by section plus production cost gives Total Cost, compared with the selling price for Profit and Markup.
Cost of one routing process per piece = Cost Of × Production Time from the Operations tab.
Named palette of colour codes (e.g. Nis_colors). Styles and materials pick one, and may only use its colours.
Named list of size codes (e.g. ERPSIZE) a style or material can use.
Number of To-UOM units in one From-UOM unit for a material. N-8: 1 KG_Nis = 1,000 meter.
Consumption unit of measure – the unit the BOM consumption is expressed in (KG_Nis for N-8).
Unit the supplier sells and invoices in. Price is entered per purchase UOM.
Unit stock is kept in after GRN.
Material quantity that covers "Cons per Item" garments. Cons Qty = Total Cons Qty ÷ Cons per Item.
Number of garments the Total Cons Qty is measured for.
Allowance for material lost in marker/cutting waste.
Process loss such as dyeing or finishing loss. It is the first step of the chain: the system turns it into a Loss Factor = 1 ÷ (1 − Loss %) and multiplies the Cons Qty by it.
Loss Factor = 1 ÷ (1 − Loss %). With 5 % loss the factor is 1.052632.
Allowance for size reduction after washing or finishing. It is the last step of the chain: Cons incl Shrinkage = Cons incl Wastage ÷ (1 − Shrinkage %).
The last figure of the consumption chain, also called the total consumption of the line: Cons × 1/(1 − Loss %), then + Wastage %, then ÷ (1 − Shrinkage %). MRP and FPO multiply quantity by it.

The final figure of the chain loss → wastage → shrinkage, i.e. Final Consumption. If only one of loss, wastage or shrinkage is filled, only that step runs and its result becomes the total consumption. Not the same as Total Cons Qty, the quantity the user enters for Cons per Item garments.
Purchase price converted to one consumption unit: Purchase Price × Conversion Factor.
Customer Supplied Value – value of material supplied by the buyer, recorded on the BOM line.
Rule mapping each garment colour to the material colour used. "Table" = mapped colour by colour; unmapped colours are [Not Used].
Rule mapping each garment size to the material size used.
Ordered list of production processes (VCutting → Sewing → VPacking) with rates and operations.
Link between a BOM material and the routing process that consumes it.
(Selling price after discount − Total cost) ÷ selling price after discount × 100.
(Selling price before discount − Total cost) ÷ Total cost × 100.
Percentage taken off the selling price before profit is calculated (10 % of 4,000 = 400).
The margin the costing aims for, shown next to Profit (21 % on Adi TShirt (NIS-59)).
Default cost rate of a sub-operation per unit of production time on the routing Operations tab.
When no material-wise UOM conversion is maintained, WFX uses factor 1 between purchase UOM and cons UOM.
Time an operation takes; Process Rate = Cost Of × Production Time.
Non-fabric materials such as sewing thread, cufflinks and polybags; each has its own techpack.
Article | Colour | Size identifier used to hold and find stock (e.g. N-8|372|34S).
RM techpack setting (e.g. ColorSize) deciding at which level stock and demand are tracked.
Projection booking used to buy long-lead material before the confirmed order.
Manually raised purchase request, here against a block booking.
MRP Level 1 indent asking production to make the garment.
MRP Level 2 indent asking purchasing to buy material for production.
Part of an indent covered by stock already in house (e.g. booking stock).
Part of an indent covered by an existing open purchase order.
Quantity not yet covered or received. Meaning depends on the document: indent (not ordered), PO (not shipped), FPPO (not received).
Minimum order / colour / size quantity rules that can round PO quantity up.
Raw Material Purchase Order placed on a supplier.
Garment Purchase Order – expected for bought-in garments; WFX currently raises an RMPO instead.
Goods Receipt Note – receipt of material against a PO at a site.
Received − Rejected. Only accepted qty becomes stock.
Confirmed buyer order. A main OC has delivery OCs, each with a colour × size breakup.
Material Requirement Planning – explodes confirmed demand level by level into production and purchase requirements.
Planning multiplier on actual requirement (1 = 100 %).
Production (make, next BOM level) or Purchase (buy, creates a PO).
Level 1 make order for an OC; decides colour quantities released to the factory.
Factory Production Order – quantity released to a specific factory.
Factory Production Process Order – one per routing process per FPO.
Stock reserved for an FPO material line.
